text:
sophia_ae: heads-up — LedgerFlow (payments fintech) wants a private POC. Requirements: no public ingress into customer VPC, allowlist all egress, must preserve client/source ip for on-prem IDS. Asking: should we recommend PrivateLink (VPCE/NLB) or TGW/peering? also need firewall port list + rough cost delta vs Dedicated for scoping.

ken_se: quick context pls: single account or multi-account? expected steady rps and peak? compliance envelope?

sophia_ae: single AWS account for now. Steady ~30rps, peaks ~250rps during settlement windows. PCI+PII in scope, strict audit + KMS rules. They insist on static outbound IPs for downstream partner allowlists.

arjun_arch: TL;DR: PrivateLink generally simpler for "no public ingress" and easier security signoff. TGW/peering gives L3 connectivity and lower hop counts but needs CIDR planning and more change control.

arjun_arch: quick tradeoffs:
- PrivateLink (NLB + VPCE): service endpoint in their VPC, no route table changes, per-service VPCE. Good when you want to keep our infra in our VPC and present an endpoint into theirs. Limited to connections to that service only (no transitive).
- TGW / VPC Peering: full network access, useful if they plan many internal integrations or want our nodes in their subnets. More blast radius and overlap checks.

maya_netops: on source IP preservation: options we use in deals:
1) Customer-run outbound proxy (recommended): they run a small forward proxy in their VPC with an EIP. We call the proxy over PrivateLink or peering; proxy forwards to on-prem, they retain final EIP and can preserve headers (X-Forwarded-For).
2) Egress from customer VPC: we place NAT/egress in their account (we can run agents there). NAT will SNAT client -> egress IP; original IP is not preserved unless they route return traffic back correctly.
3) BGP/VPN asymmetry: if they want raw client IP visible on-prem without a proxy, they must accept asymmetric routing and configure route back to our collectors — operationally brittle.

ken_se: firewall snippet we can paste into security questionnaire?

arjun_arch: yes, send this minimal copy/paste block:

```
# LedgerFlow firewall egress snippet for Redwood private POC
- Protocol: TCP
- Ports: 443
- Destination: <VPCE subnet CIDR> OR <Redwood EIP set>
- Description: Redwood Inference private endpoints / egress
# Optional: allow TCP 8000-8010 from Redwood control plane IPs for healthchecks (confirm exact list with ops)
```

maya_netops: TLS inspection note: if they TLS-inspect, request they whitelist SNI for our hostnames or use passthrough. If mutual TLS is required for control-plane APIs, we need cert exchange ahead of time.

sophia_ae: cost guidance for scoping (ballpark only):
- Dedicated: reserved GPU pool + Redwood platform — e.g., for this load maybe a 4-GPU reserved pool estimate ~$9k-12k/month (depends on model, batching).
- Private: platform license + customer infra. Typical onboarding fee ~$25k-40k + annual platform fee; infra charged in their account (GPUs/instances). Have finance produce formal quote.

arjun_arch: blockers to surface in presales call:
- overlapping CIDRs if TGW/peering chosen (ask for their full CIDR list)
- strict egress allowlist policies that reject periodic IP changes (we can publish IPs but ops cadence may be needed)
- requirement for inbound admin/control plane access to our management endpoints (we can offer VPN or customer-managed control plane variants)

maya_netops: also confirm KMS/HSM requirements and cloudtrail/audit log retention. If they require an airgapped management plane, that's a separate Private engagement.

ops-bot: reminder: create handoff invite and attach security questionnaire to shared drive.

sophia_ae: next steps: scheduling 30m tech handoff w/ LedgerFlow + netops tomorrow 9:30am PT. @arjun_arch @maya_netops can you join? I'll ask them to provide a proposed list of static EIPs prior to the call.

arjun_arch: I'll join.

maya_netops: available.

sophia_ae: thanks team — I'll send the invite and paste the firewall snippet in the questionnaire. :thumbsup:
